A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations and calibration experiments with Genie2, ESM3, TarFlow, and Gemma-2-9B-IT, including supplementary analyses and generated samples.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical applications and reports additional rare-event experiments and augmented-Lagrangian comparisons in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The original CGM-relax and CGM-reward procedures remain unchanged. Appendix E adds an auxiliary calibration variant, CGM-AL, adapting augmented Lagrangian optimization through stochastic parameter updates and periodic dual-variable updates, with pseudocode in Algorithm 3.

E1.justification: v4 adds a rare-event scenario that halves the probability of an already-rare Gaussian-mixture mode. The earlier task of upweighting that mode to 0.8 remains in Appendix F.1. Protein, image, language, and high-dimensional mixture coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Appendix E and Figure 7 introduce CGM-AL as an evaluated optimization comparator across both rare-event scenarios and the increasing-constraint experiment. This substantially extends the synthetic comparisons beyond the original CGM methods and reference distributions. Khalifa et al. (2021) remains the language-model baseline.

E3.justification: The new multiplicative rare-event experiment uses normalized relative error, 5,000 constant-step updates, and a six-point log(lambda) search over [-3,2] selecting minimum error. Retained simulations use 2,000 updates and the 90%-reduction selection rule. The fixed-target rarity sweep also ends near 10^-4 instead of 10^-5, and CGM-AL adds a dual-update-frequency search.

E4.justification: Rare-event robustness analysis now includes reducing already-rare modes, keeping rare samples scarce throughout fine-tuning. Existing hyperparameter sweeps, oracle-reward comparisons, protein sampling controls, image failure examples, and held-out profession analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 specifies a two-sided t-test for the previously reported significant improvement over Khalifa et al. (2021). Appendix F.1 also documents delta-method error bars for log-scale KL estimates. Existing replicate counts and two-standard-error reporting are retained; no increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: v4 reports new halving-task results: approximately 80–90% error reduction at rarity 10^-2 and 50% at 10^-3. Figure 7 adds mixed CGM-AL outcomes: better constraint satisfaction on multiplicative rare-event calibration, worse on fixed-target calibration, and comparable high-dimensional performance. These extend the results under distinct settings; the principal application results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (8)'s constant is corrected from E[exp(r)] to log E[exp(r)]. The proofs of Theorem C.3 and Proposition C.5 add absolute values around q in integrability conditions. Appendix E introduces augmented-Lagrangian and dual formulations; existing unbiasedness, convergence, and diffusion results are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain two calibration objectives demonstrated across three applications. The introduction replaces v2's claim that neither prior method removes most calibration error with a comparison emphasizing restricted model classes and low-dimensional validation, while acknowledging concurrent primal-dual work.

C2.justification: v4 recommends trying CGM-reward first under compute constraints, followed by a CGM-relax grid search if needed. It adds interpretations of seed-dependent rare-event failures, explains the practical preference for CGM-relax over CGM-AL despite mixed results, and discusses the upfront computation advantage of fine-tuning over inference-time constraints.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 newly specifies synthetic learning rates, including the 10^-3 to 10^-6 schedule for retained experiments. Appendix E documents CGM-AL implementation and hyperparameter searches. The application configurations in Table 1, hardware disclosure, LoRA details, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds the distinct Khalafi et al. (2026) work and expands connections to density estimation, ensemble biasing, and inference-time methods, including Efron and Tibshirani, Pitera and Chodera, Kolloff, Liu, and Yao. These additions refine the existing positioning around broadly applicable generative-model fine-tuning.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the method exposition, simulation narrative, and language-model case study are rewritten or condensed. Appendix A is reorganized, the experimental appendix moves from E to F around the new comparison appendix, and an Author Contributions section is added. The full language-model prompt remains available in the appendix.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays. Figure 3 reverses the metric-panel order and introduces logarithmic KL scaling for rare events. v4 adds Figure 7 and Algorithm 3; earlier appendix figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added relative-error rare-event test and CGM-AL comparison strengthen robustness and comparative evidence. Clearer experimental settings, statistical procedures, and the log-normalizer correction improve reproducibility and precision. Appendix E's broad 'no better' summary overstates its mixed comparator results, but the detailed evidence still supports a limited net improvement; the principal application findings remain unchanged.
